title: Console: Retention Settings (v1) — Wireframes + UX Notes
content:
Slide 1 — Title
Console: Retention Settings (v1)
Wireframes + UX Notes (Draft)
Owner: Kenji Nakamura (UX)
Collaborators: Nora Ahmed, Tessa Morgan, Chloe Martin, Jada Williams, Felix Schneider, Naomi Feldman
Last updated: 2025-02-18

Slide 2 — Context / Why this page exists
Problem:
- Enterprise security reviews repeatedly ask “how long do you keep X?”, “can we change retention?”, “how do you enforce it?”, “can we prove it?”
- Today we have partial answers spread across docs; Console needs a canonical place for tenant admins.

This deck covers UI for:
1) Retention Settings page (configure + view effective policy)
2) Enforcement Status panel (auditability + operational confidence)
3) Exceptions / Legal Hold UX
4) Admin audit trail for retention changes

Non-goals (v1):
- Per-stream retention across all infra logs (SRE/vendor constrained)
- Customer-configurable retention for raw inference payload content (handled separately)

Slide 3 — Design principles (for review)
- Safe defaults: show current policy + guardrails before letting users change anything
- Explain “effective policy”: users shouldn’t need to know precedence rules to trust what will happen
- Auditability: every change generates an admin audit event; page surfaces last enforcement + exceptions
- Avoid false promises: label datasets that are “not configurable in v1” clearly and explain why
- Minimize fear: retention changes can be scary; include clear warnings and when changes take effect

Slide 4 — Information Architecture (Console)
Proposed nav placement:
Console → Security & Compliance → Data Retention
Secondary links:
- Audit Logs (existing area) gets deep-link to retention section
- Compliance Reporting Pack (future link) could live in same Security & Compliance category

Page sections (top to bottom):
A) Summary banner: “Effective retention by dataset” + last updated
B) Dataset retention table/cards: configure where allowed
C) Enforcement status: last run, errors, backlog, per-dataset enforcement method
D) Legal holds + exceptions: active holds, request workflow (links)
E) Admin audit trail (embedded table) + link to full Audit Log filter view

Slide 5 — Page header / Summary banner (wireframe)
[Header]
Data Retention
Control how long Redwood retains operational and security-relevant data for your organization.

[Environment selector]  Production | Staging (if enabled)
[Region selector]  US-East | EU-West (shown only for multi-region tenants)

[Summary banner]
Effective retention (Production, US-East)
- Audit logs: 365 days
- Admin activity: 365 days
- Inference request metadata: 30 days
- Telemetry / analytics: 90 days
- Operational logs (SRE-managed): Fixed (14 days)

Banner footnote text:
“Effective retention reflects all applicable policies and legal holds. Learn more → (docs link)”

Speaker notes:
- Goal: immediately answer the 5 most common datasets.
- “Operational logs” explicitly called out as not configurable.

Slide 6 — Dataset list (table view option)
Option A: Table (compact, enterprise-friendly)
Columns:
- Dataset
- Retention (Effective)
- Configurable
- Enforcement method
- Status
- Actions

Row example:
Dataset: Audit logs
Retention (Effective): 365 days
Configurable: Yes
Enforcement method: Scheduled deletion + partition TTL (where supported)
Status: Healthy
Actions: View details | Edit

Row example (not configurable):
Dataset: Operational logs (node/system)
Retention (Effective): 14 days
Configurable: No
Enforcement method: Vendor/SRE standard
Status: —
Actions: Learn why

Speaker notes:
- The “Status” column should map to enforcement job health signals (ENG-2944).
- “Learn why” opens a side panel with explanation + recommended alternatives.

Slide 7 — Dataset details (card/accordion view option)
Option B: Cards/accordions (more explanatory)
Each dataset card shows:
- Name + description
- Effective retention (big number)
- “Configured by” line (who/what set it)
- Guardrails (min/max)
- Enforcement method
- Last enforcement run
- Edit button (if allowed)

Card example: Inference request metadata
Description: “Metadata about requests (timestamps, model, token counts, latency). Does not include prompt/response bodies.”
Effective retention: 30 days
Configured by: Org policy (default)
Guardrails: Min 7 days, Max 365 days
Enforcement: Partition TTL
Last enforcement: 2025-02-16 03:10 UTC
[Edit]

Speaker notes:
- This view helps reduce confusion about what’s included/excluded.
- Copy must be vetted with Security/Compliance for accuracy.

Slide 8 — “Configured by” / Precedence explanation (effective policy)
In dataset details panel, show an “Effective policy breakdown” component:
Effective retention: 90 days
Derived from:
1) Legal hold: none
2) Tenant override (Production, US-East): 90 days (set Feb 12, 2025 by Naomi Feldman)
3) Org default: 30 days

UI element: “Why 90 days?” link opens breakdown drawer.
Drawer content:
- Policy sources and scopes (Org, Tenant, Environment, Region)
- Applied rule: “Most specific scope wins; legal hold overrides deletion.”
- Link: “View change in Audit Log”

Speaker notes:
- Users need confidence that the system will do what it says.
- Keep rule language simple; full schema stays in docs.

Slide 9 — Edit retention flow (modal)
Edit button opens modal:
Title: Edit retention — Telemetry / analytics
Fields:
- Retention duration: [ 90 ] [days dropdown]
- Scope: Production (fixed based on page env selector)
- Region: US-East (if multi-region)

Guardrails section:
Allowed range: 30–400 days (example)

Warnings:
- “Reducing retention may permanently delete older records after enforcement runs.”
- “Retention changes apply going forward; some backends enforce within up to 24 hours.”

Buttons:
Cancel | Save changes

Secondary (advanced) link:
“Request exception / legal hold” (takes user to exceptions section)

Slide 10 — Validation & error states (modal)
Inline errors:
- “Must be at least 7 days.”
- “Must be no more than 365 days.”
- “This dataset is not configurable for your deployment type.”

Save behavior:
- On save: confirmation toast “Retention updated. Enforcement will apply within 24 hours.”
- Also show a non-dismissible inline success summary on dataset card for 60 minutes:
  “Updated Feb 18, 2025 by Kenji Nakamura (via Console)”

Permission states:
- If user lacks admin permission: disable Edit + show tooltip “Requires Org Admin (Security & Compliance).”

Speaker notes:
- RBAC check maps to Console roles; verify with Kaitlyn Nguyen.

Slide 11 — Legal hold banner (page-level)
When ANY legal hold is active:
[Banner - warning]
Legal hold active
Some datasets may be retained beyond your configured retention settings. View holds →

When user tries to reduce retention while legal hold exists:
- Allow saving the configured retention value, but show:
  “Note: legal hold prevents deletion for affected datasets until released.”

Speaker notes:
- Legal hold should not block “configuration,” only block enforcement deletion.

Slide 12 — Exceptions & legal holds section (wireframe)
Section title: Exceptions & legal holds

Subsection A: Active legal holds
Table:
- Hold ID
- Scope (datasets)
- Reason
- Created by
- Created at
- Status
- Actions (View)

Subsection B: Retention exceptions
Text:
“Need retention outside allowed ranges? Submit a request. Exceptions require Security + Legal approval and are reviewed quarterly.”
Buttons:
- Submit request (opens form / links to internal process for now)
- View policy docs

Speaker notes:
- For v1, “Submit request” can deep-link to support workflow / internal process doc.
- Long-term: in-product workflow with approvals.

Slide 13 — Enforcement status panel (overview)
Section title: Enforcement status
Goal: show “we actually delete data” without exposing sensitive infrastructure details.

Panel contents:
- Overall status: Healthy / Degraded / Delayed
- Last successful enforcement run: timestamp
- Next scheduled run: timestamp
- Backlog estimate: “Oldest pending deletion candidate: 2025-01-20”
- Recent errors: count (last 24h) + link to status details

CTA links:
- “View detailed status” (drawer)
- “Download enforcement attestation (PDF)” (future; ties to reporting pack)

Slide 14 — Enforcement status details drawer
Drawer sections:
1) Per-dataset enforcement method
- Audit logs: deletion worker (batch deletes)
- Telemetry: partition TTL
- Admin activity: deletion worker
- Operational logs: fixed (vendor/SRE)

2) Metrics (read-only)
- Delete throughput (records/hr)
- Error rate
- Max DB load cap hit (yes/no)

3) Last 10 runs (table)
- Run ID
- Started
- Completed
- Result
- Records deleted
- Notes (e.g., “throttled due to load”) 

Speaker notes:
- This panel can map to ENG-2944 dashboards, but presented in customer-safe terms.
- Avoid exposing table names, cluster IDs, or vendor internals.

Slide 15 — Degraded states (copy)
State: Delayed
Copy:
“Enforcement is delayed. Your configured retention remains in effect; deletion may occur later than usual. We are monitoring this and will catch up automatically.”

State: Degraded
Copy:
“Some datasets may not be enforcing retention due to an operational issue. Contact support if you need a compliance attestation for a specific date range.”

State: Healthy
Copy:
“Retention enforcement is running normally.”

Speaker notes:
- Copy is intentionally conservative; reviewed with SRE to avoid SLA commitments.

Slide 16 — Admin audit trail (embedded)
Section title: Retention changes (admin audit trail)

Embedded table (filter preset):
- Time
- Actor
- Action
- Dataset
- Old value
- New value
- Scope (env/region)
- Source (Console / API)
- Event ID

Row example:
2025-02-18 10:22 UTC | Kenji Nakamura | Update retention policy | Telemetry/analytics | 30d | 90d | Production/US-East | Console | aud_01H…

Actions:
- View in Audit Logs (opens Audit Log viewer filtered to event)
- Export CSV (respecting retention limits)

Slide 17 — Audit event “diff” view (detail drawer)
When clicking an event row:
Drawer title: Retention policy updated
Fields:
- Event ID
- Actor (user id + email)
- Auth method (SSO / API key)
- IP address (if available)
- Timestamp

Diff block (human readable):
- Dataset: Telemetry/analytics
- Scope: Production / US-East
- Retention: 30 days → 90 days
- Reason: (optional free text)

Speaker notes:
- Reason field is optional; consider requiring for decreases.

Slide 18 — API/Automation alignment (UX notes)
UX should assume changes may come from API as well as Console.
- In tables/cards show “Source: Console” or “Source: API”
- If a policy is managed externally (API), show subtle callout:
  “This setting is managed via API. You can edit here, but changes may be overwritten by automation.” (open question)

Open question:
- Do we need an explicit “lock” concept to avoid tug-of-war? (Probably later)

Slide 19 — Deployment mode nuances (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
Hosted:
- Default retention values apply; tenant can configure eligible datasets
- Enforcement status visible

Dedicated:
- Same UI; some backends may differ but we keep customer-facing method labels consistent

Private (VPC/on-prem):
- Enforcement status might be reported by local control plane
- Some features may be “Not available in this deployment” depending on installed version

Copy pattern:
“Availability depends on your deployment configuration. Contact your admin or Redwood support.”

Slide 20 — Copy draft: dataset descriptions (v1)
Audit logs
“Security-relevant events about actions taken in Redwood (e.g., user access, configuration changes).”

Admin activity
“Administrative actions within the Console, including retention changes and access management.”

Inference request metadata
“Request metadata (timestamps, model, token counts, latency). Excludes prompt/response bodies.”

Telemetry / analytics
“Aggregated and event-level product telemetry used for performance and usage analytics. Excludes customer payload content.”

Operational logs
“System/service logs used to operate the platform. Retention is managed by Redwood SRE standards and vendor constraints.”

Speaker notes:
- Needs alignment with Telemetry team (Logan/Nadia) and Security (Marcus/Kevin).

Slide 21 — Open questions / decisions needed
1) Default retention values by tier (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) — confirm with Product/Compliance
2) Guardrails min/max per dataset — confirm with policy guardrails group
3) “Reason” requirement — do we require for decreases? (security review friendly)
4) “Managed by API” behavior — warning only vs introduce lock
5) Enforcement status depth — how much can we show without leaking infra details?

Slide 22 — Engineering notes (handoff)
Primary implementation touchpoints:
- Retention settings API endpoints (ENG-2926)
- Legal hold + exceptions flags (ENG-2934)
- Audit events on changes (Console + Control Plane)
- Enforcement status surface (ties to ENG-2944 dashboards)

UI components needed:
- Dataset table/cards
- Effective policy breakdown drawer
- Edit retention modal + validation
- Enforcement status panel + details drawer
- Embedded audit trail table + event detail drawer

Slide 23 — Next steps
- Review with Naomi Feldman (product) + Marcus Lin (security eng) for copy + dataset definitions
- Validate with Console eng on feasibility of enforcement status fields available in v1
- Update wireframes with final default values + guardrail ranges
- Align with reporting pack outputs (future: “download attestation”)

Appendix — Notes to self (Kenji)
- Avoid saying “guarantee deletion by X hours” anywhere
- Make sure “request metadata” definition is consistent with what we store today (do not over-claim)
- Add a subtle link to “Data residency” page if/when it exists in Console
